title.narrative: Improving the Core Functions of Primary Care in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative:
WP1: To develop the PCAT in appropriate languages with support for data collection, analysis and reporting.
• WP2: To measure the core functions of primary care in eleven sub-Saharan African countries.
• WP3: Engagement with local and regional stakeholders

recipient-country.narrative: IN Botswana the PCAT Study is led by Dr Keneilwe Motlhatlhedi, a Family Physician and lecturer at the University of Botswana. She is currently pursuing a Master of Clinical epidemiology at the University of Pennsylvania

In Benin the PCAT study is led by Dr Kéfilath Bello, a Public Health Medical Doctor who also works as a research fellow at the 'Centre de recherche en Reproduction Humaine et en Démographie’ (CERRHUD) since June 2015. Her research work focuses on human resource management and quality improvement strategies for improving primary health care. She obtained her PhD in General Practice

In Kenya, the PCAT study is led by Dr Gulnaz Mohamoud, a Senior Lecturer in Family Medicine at Aga Khan University, Kenya. She completed her PhD in 2022, which was focused on evaluating the performance of 13 private sector primary care clinics in Nairobi. In doing this she adapted and validated the PCAT for Kenya using a national panel of experts. In this project, she would focus on using the PCAT to measure primary care performance in the public sector of Kenya and sharing her expertise with the regional team.

In Lesotho, the PCAT study is led by Dr Sebaka Malope, the Director of the Lesotho-Boston Health Alliance (LeBoHA) Family Medicine Specialty Training Program in Lesotho and Assistant Professor at Boston University School of Medicine.

In Malawi, the PCAT study is led by Dr Luckson Dullie, the Executive Director at Partners in Health Malawi and a clinical lecturer in the Department of Family Medicine at Kamuzu University of Health Sciences. As part of his PhD through the University of Bergen, he developed the Malawian version of the PCAT

In Namibia the PCAT study is led Dr Felicia Christian, an associate Dean at school of Medicine, University of Namibia. She is an experienced Family Physician and an academic leader with over 40 years’ experience in clinical practice, public health, and medical education (undergraduate and postgraduate). She has a proven track record in curriculum development, program leadership, research, and health systems strengthening, with a passion for improving healthcare delivery in underserved and rural communities, particularly in non-communicable disease management.

In Nigeria the PCAT study is led by Dr Bola Fatusin, a Consultant Family Physician and Academic Coordinator in the Family Medicine Department at the Federal Medical Centre in Gusau, Nigeria. She is an emerging leader in the AfriWon Research Collaborative (ARC), an online research mentorship and training programme for AfriWon Renaissance members in Africa that aims to increase research activity through an e-learning community.
In Tanzania, the PCAT study is led by A/Prof Riaz Ratansi, based at the Aga Khan University in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania and Head of the Department of Family Medicine.

In Uganda, the PCAT study is led by Dr Innocent Besigye, a Senior Lecturer in Family Medicine at Makerere University. He has adapted and validated the PCAT for Uganda as part of his PhD and added items to measure the construct of patient-centredness. He has subsequently shown in Tororo District how the findings can be workshopped with district-level stakeholders to design, develop and implement interventions to improve primary care performance. In this project, he would focus on using the PCAT to measure primary care performance in another district of Uganda and sharing his expertise with the regional team. He is also on the executive of PRIMAFAMED, Wonca Africa and part of the leadership of the AfroPHC Forum with good links to WHO Afro.

In Zambia the PCAT study is led by Dr Mpundu Makasa, a clinician and public health practitioner who works in the primary health care setting and affiliated with the University of Zambia. She has a Master of Public Health and a PhD in Epidemiology.

South Africa is the lead country hosting the PCAT study and led by the UCT team under Assoc Prof Von Pressentin head of the Division of Family Medicine at the University of Cape Town (UCT). Prof Von Pressentin has used the PCAT to evaluate primary care performance in South Africa in a study comparing facilities with and without family physicians as part of his PhD. He is the Editor-in-Chief of the South African Family Practice Journal. His research focuses on primary care service strengthening (including chronic conditions and palliative care in primary care), human resources for health, as well as health professions education. He teaches primary care research methods, leadership development, clinical governance, evidence-based practice, and consultation skills.
He is co-leading with Prof Bob Mash the Executive Head of the Department of Family and Emergency Medicine and Divisional Head of the Division of Family Medicine and Primary Care at Stellenbosch University. He is an established primary care researcher in the African region and internationally recognized (for example he was elected as a member of the USA National Academy of Medicine). He is also the coordinator of the PRIMAFAMED network and editor-in-chief of the African Journal of Primary Health Care and Family Medicine. Dr Robin Dyers (PhD) is a Public Health Specialist for the Chief Directorate: Health Programmes, Western Cape Government: Health and Wellness, and has an extraordinary appointment at Stellenbosch University’s Division of Health Systems and Public Health (Department of Global Health, Stellenbosch University). His special interests include health information systems, business analysis, morbidity surveillance and health-related concept encoding. Dr Dyers does research in Design Science, Health Information Systems and User Experience Design. Their current project is 'A User Experience Model for the Visualisation of Routine Health Information System Data for Managerial Decision Support. Dr Edith Madela-Mntla is the Community Engagement Lead from Pretoria University
